files.content: # Archive light table — Style Prompt > Archive objects (glass negatives, slides, clippings, letters) lie on a cool, backlit light table under one camera. The camera glides across the table and slows; a loupe drops onto one plate, crop corners grow around the frame the photograph will open to, and inside the glass the negative turns positive from the centre out. Then the camera dives through the lens until the photograph fills the frame and gains depth: the near ground swells, the subject drifts forward. Ink leaders with a signal-coloured anchor pin a serif title and a name to the picture, and dark caption plates carry the words. Clean, quiet and modern: the age is in the objects, never in a filter. ## 1. Essence, and what it is not - **One world, one camera.** Every object lies on the table with a centre, a rotation and a size, and the camera reaches it by gliding. There are no cuts, fades to black or page turns between objects: every transition is the glide or the loupe (land, dive in, rise out, lift). - **Light comes from below.** The table glows a near-white cool grey; glass transmits it, so a negative reads as a dark plate whose broken corner shows the table; paper reads as a light sheet with ink. - **The loupe is the camera's door.** Every dive goes through a loupe that lands on the object. Inside the lens is where the object changes state: negative to positive, one line lit, a figure lifted out. - **Catalogue truth.** Every object carries a number, a title and an identifier printed on the table above it (`03 Hari pertama, 1958 ARS-58-003`). Figures on screen come from the record and quote their source under them. - **One signal colour** for anchors, crop corners, readouts and plate edges; everything else is the archive's own greys and paper tones. - **Real or drawn, never faked.** When the user has scans of their own photographs, letters or ledgers (their uploaded media), lay those on the table with their own identifiers. Without scans, draw the objects as the example does, as illustrations, and never pass a drawn picture off as a real record of a real institution. Not a halftone dossier (no newsprint dots, no aged-paper grade), not sepia or a vintage filter, not a slideshow of photos cut together, not a data story (no charts: numbers live on the objects or on one reading plate), not a stage talk (no slides, no header bars). ## 2. Materials & rendering - **The table**: near-white (about #f7f9fb lit), a very gentle falloff toward its far edges (−14% at the frame of the panel) and faint diffuser noise (±0.5% at about 20 px, ±0.6% at about 140 px). Dust is fixed to the table: dense small dark specks (about one per 100 × 100 px at landing zoom, 1-4 px, darkening by about 30%), one SVG path that travels with the table. A screen vignette darkens the corners by about 10%. - **Glass negatives**: transmission from the positive, `T = 0.035 + 0.9 · (1 − pos)^1.25`, tinted warm silver (0.98, 0.93, 0.84). In 2D, one canvas filter pass at load (`invert(1) brightness(0.86) sepia(0.28)` plus a 0.8 px blur) gives the same curve within a few percent. The emulsion edge is a clip-path polygon jittered ±3 px every 46 px; a broken corner of five or six shards shows the table through it. - **Prints**: drawn once to canvas in print tones from a lifted black (about 4%) to a warm white (0.99, 0.98, 0.96): hazy sky, a soft line of far trees on the horizon, sand with patches and tracks, speckle that grows toward the viewer. For the photograph space they are separate layers with a nearness `n` (0 at the horizon, rising linearly below it): sky 0, ground 0.3, near ground 0.75 (with a soft top edge), each upright subject at the nearness of its ground line. - **The loupe** (lens radius R, 300 px at landing zoom): a near-black ring from 1.0 to 1.065 R with two thin bevel highlights lit from the upper left; a clear acrylic skirt from 1.065 to 1.30 R that shows the table a little darker on light and a little lighter on dark (a mid-grey at 7%), with a dark line on its inner edge, a bright hairline near its outer edge, a dark hairline at the edge, and a soft shadow ring just outside. Inside: the object at 2.5× its table size, the rim darkened 30% from 0.78 R, two faint speculars at (−0.38, −0.46) R and (0.42, 0.50) R. A lifted loupe (scale 1.35) casts a shadow offset down and right, 22% dark; it tightens to nothing as it lands. - **Marks**: anchor rings (radius 9 px, 2 px signal stroke) with a 3 px signal dot; leaders in ink, 1.5 px; crop corners 2.6 px in the signal colour; readout leaders 2 px in the signal colour. - **Post**: moving film grain (±1.8% per pixel, +1.6% more inside a photograph; in 2D one noise image re-placed every frame) and the light vignette. No film damage, no sepia, no halftone. - **2D, never live 3D**: depth from layer scale and shift by nearness, light from gradients, the negative from a filter pass at load. Draw every texture once and only move it; repaint only while the camera dives. ## 3. Colour logic - `--latar` is the light table; `--latar-2` its dimmer edge. A dark brand switches the table off: the plates glow on a dark desk, which still reads because the archive tones never follow the brand. - `--utama` is the one signal colour: anchor rings and dots, crop corners, readout leaders, the left edge of every caption and reading plate, and the chips behind magnification and dates (`×2,5`, `1958.03.15`) with `--teks-di-utama` text. Never a fill behind a picture, never decoration. - `--utama-di-latar` is the catalogue number printed on the table (`03`, `04`); `--teks` the catalogue title; `--teks-redup` the identifier. - `--aksen` is only the warm edge of the develop front (a 6 px ring at 75%). - Fixed in every brand: the archive's tones (print tone, negative silver, newsprint), ink for titles, names, leaders and credits set on a print, paper white for text on caption plates, the caption plate itself (near-black at 74-78%), the loupe ring. Text on a print is ink on its light sky or sand; text over glass or a dark area sits on a caption plate. Never colour on colour. ## 4. Type - `--font-judul` carries the one title a photograph wears (Libre Baskerville 700 at 64 px for a 1920 wide frame) and the name on the closing plate (54 px). When the brand has none: Libre Baskerville 700, Cormorant Garamond 700 or Playfair Display 700. - `--font-isi` carries labels and plates: the fact line under a title (25 px), a name label (28 px, 600), the caption line (36-40 px, 600) with its second line (26-27 px), catalogue titles (21-26 px, 600), the reading label (26 px) and unit (44 px). - A look token, `--font-kode` (IBM Plex Mono 400 and 600), carries identifiers, dates, the magnification readout (30 px), the second line of a name label (19 px), credits' identifiers and the reading figure (118 px). A brand never replaces it. - Labels attach to objects: anchor, leader, tick, then text aligned to the leader's x, left or right. Text wipes in from its leader side. - Caption plates sit bottom centre, as wide as their text plus 56 px, two lines (main, then source or translation), never wrapped: split a long sentence into two cues. ## 5. Motion quality - One beat = 2/3 s at the reference's pace; every key action sits on a beat or half-beat. All camera values run on monotone cubic curves (Fritsch–Carlson) through keys: centre, log zoom and roll. No overshoot, no stepping. - **Glide**: from one object to the next in about 1.4 s, zoom easing out (0.66 → 0.30), roll levelling from −4° to −1.6°. - **Loupe landing**: 0.4 s before its beat, cubic out, scale 1.35 → 1 and opacity on the same curve; lifting is the mirror, 0.4 s after its beat, opacity on smoothstep. - **Crop corners**: arms grow from each corner of the photograph's 16:9 frame (960 × 540 px at landing) on cubic in-out, from 0.5 s before landing to 0.2 s after, opacity ×1.5; they retract 0.2-0.7 s after the dive starts. - **Readout**: a leader from 1.34 R at −56° out 70 px, then 46 px level; `×2,5` and the state below it fade in 0.05-0.4 s after landing; the state crossfades to `negatif → positif` over 0.3 s on the develop beat; all of it leaves 0.3-0.7 s after the dive starts. - **Develop**: half a beat after landing, 0.8 s cubic in-out; the front grows from the centre to 1.25 R with a thin warm edge that fades in between 0.05 and 0.35 R. - **Dive**: 2.0 s, zoom ×4.3 (0.335 → 1.45), roll −1° → 0°; the view inside widens from 2.5× the table to two thirds of that scale, so the photograph lands at rest just as the rim leaves the frame; depth fades in from 0.5 s into the dive to the landing. - **Photograph space**: over the whole stay (4.7 s), depth `p` on smoothstep: each layer scales by `1 + 0.55 · p · (n − n_focus)` and shifts by `(260, −140) · p · (n − n_focus)` units about the view centre, so the near sand swells to about 1.3× while the sky shrinks; the subject drifts 125 units forward and 26 up on cubic in-out; the view centre pans 120 units and the scale grows 7%. - **Annotations**: on the beat the anchor ring grows in 0.25 s; the ink leader rises 80-140 px from 0.08 to 0.4 s, then a 34 px tick from 0.4 to 0.6 s; the text block wipes in from 0.35 to 0.85 s (cubic out). A second label follows a beat later (0.6 s), the credit 0.4 s after the title. Everything leaves 0.35 s after the rise starts, in 0.3 s. - **Reading plate**: a dark plate wipes in from its edge in 0.45 s; the figure counts up and lands on its beat; held at least 1.5 s. - **Rise out**: zoom back to the table in 1 s while the centre glides to the next object; the loupe, still showing the photograph, slides off one side and lifts. - **Holds**: captions at least max(1.8 s, the sentence + 0.6 s), fading 0.12 s each way; the closing at least 2 s with the camera still. - What never moves: the archive's content outside the photograph space, and the table itself. ## 6. Camera grammar | Move | What it expresses | Can serve | |---|---|---| | Table glide (pan with ≤ 4° roll, zoom easing out) | surveying; moving to the next piece of evidence | a timeline of documents, a product family, an album | | Loupe landing (1.35× → 1×, crop corners growing) | choosing one object; "look closer" | the claim, the key photograph, a signature | | Slow push (zoom 0.30 → 0.335) | attention narrowing before a reveal | the line before the dive, a detail | | Dive through the lens (×4.3, rim leaves the frame) | entering the moment | the founding day, the event, the place | | Photograph dolly with nearness parallax | being there | the people, the first shop, the crowd | | Rise out of the lens while gliding on | the evidence noted; on to the next | a change of era, the next chapter | | Pull back to the whole table (zoom to about 0.09) | everything at once | an index, a timeline, a closing | Framing: at a reading moment the subject fills at least a third of the frame height, and titles, labels and readings stay clear of the caption plate (the bottom 200 px). Land the loupe straight onto the object; glide over objects, never over empty table. ## 7. Native moves - **Negative to positive under the loupe.** A develop front spreads from the lens centre with a thin warm edge and turns the glass negative into its positive only inside the lens; the readout beside it changes from `negatif` to `negatif → positif`. *Fits content like:* a barbershop's first day under a tree; a founder's portrait plate; a school's first class photo for its anniversary; the lost photograph a family story turns on. - **The dive into the photograph.** A slow push, then the rim grows past the frame while the view inside widens, until the photograph fills the screen; the near ground swells and the subject drifts forward. *Fits content like:* the first kiosk on the street; a creator's first studio corner; the field where a village team first played; the harbour in a grandfather's story. - **Pinned title and name.** An anchor ring lands on the subject, an ink leader rises and ticks sideways, a serif title and a fact line wipe in from it; a second, smaller label pins a name or an object a beat later. *Fits content like:* "Karto Wiryo · pemangkas · 1 kursi · 1 cermin"; a bakery's first oven; a teacher's first classroom; the captain of a fishing boat in a short story. - **The reading plate.** One dark plate beside the subject: a small label, a big mono figure that counts up, and the source's own wording under it. *Fits content like:* customers on day one from the cash book; the first print run of a zine; students in a course's first batch; the days a letter took to arrive. - **The line lights up.** On a document inside the lens one line brightens left to right while the rest dims, an underline draws under it, and one figure is ringed and lifted into a reading plate. *Fits content like:* the first entry in a ledger; a recipe card's secret quantity; a report card's grade; the date at the top of a love letter. - **Measuring on the photograph.** A ruler laid on the ground plane in perspective, ticks crowding toward the horizon, a counter that lands on the recorded figure. *Fits content like:* the length of a market street; the distance a delivery bike rode; a school's running track; the river crossing in a story. - **Two records, held side by side.** Two caption plates, each with a crop of its source, held still until both are read before one is struck. *Fits content like:* two founding dates in two family stories; the price list of 1975 against today's; a draft and the published version of a creator's script. - **The table becomes the index.** Pull back to the whole table; each object's catalogue tag flies into one list with its identifier and its reading. *Fits content like:* a company's timeline; a channel's milestones; a course syllabus as artefacts; the chapters of a memoir. ## 8. Pitfalls - **Performance (live preview).** Draw prints, negatives, paper and grain once (canvas, then ``), with one blur or filter pass per canvas, never per stroke. Per frame only transforms change: the table, the lens window and its content, the photograph layers, the ring, the marks; the develop clip runs for one second. Keep the table and the lens composited (`will-change: transform`) except while the camera dives, so they stay sharp; hide the table, ring and table marks while the lens covers the frame. - **Over-magnifying.** Keep the photograph layers at about one pixel per screen pixel in the photograph space; the negative may be softer, it is only glimpsed. - **The loupe over empty table.** Lay objects close, land the loupe straight onto its object, glide over objects, never over gaps. - **Labels that scroll away.** Hold the camera while a label is read, or fix the caption on screen. Labels on a photograph follow its layers but keep their size; catalogue tags keep a near-constant size (camera scale clamped to 0.45-1.6). - **Shear and holes.** Each parallax layer must extend beyond the frame by the amount it shrinks or shifts; a near-ground layer needs a soft top edge, and no layer may leave an unfilled strip (it becomes a black line once encoded). - **Text on a print.** Only ink on its light sky or sand, kept clear of dark areas such as a tree canopy; everything else goes on a caption plate. - **Vintage creep.** No sepia, no halftone, no ageing overlay, no film damage: the age is in the objects. - **Honesty.** Drawn objects are illustrations; catalogue numbers are the user's own or plainly invented for the story, never a real archive's. ## Measured from the reference One continuous shot of 12 s, no cuts, moderate motion; it is the middle of a longer piece. Its beats, scaled by 1.25 for a 15 s video: the glide ends and the loupe lands 0.12-0.62 s; crop corners 0-0.87 s; the readout 0.68-1.12 s; develop 1.04-2.04 s; the dive 2.29-4.79 s (the rim at about 75% of the frame height at 3.75 s); the photograph space 4.79-10.62 s with its caption at 5.2 s, the title at 5.6 s, the second label at 6.4 s, the next caption at 8.85 s; the rise 10.62 s; the loupe lands on the next plate at about 12.3 s (13.1 s in the reference, pulled forward here so the ending holds 2.6 s). Palette of the reference: table #e9eaed on screen (#f7f9fb lit), glass negative #2d2b27 to #5d5950, print sky #bbb9b5, horizon #858381, ground #696763 to #888683, loupe ring #141211, signal #ff5a1f, caption plates rgba(14,15,17,0.74). ## Variation space The assistant decides the objects, their order, the story, which native moves to spend and where, the camera path and the subject of the photograph space. - **Structures**: a business's founding told as four or five objects in date order, each dive revealing one person; a single photograph explored in three dives (the place, the people, the date written on the back); a before-and-after pair of plates of one street. - **Openings**: the table switching on in the dark (flickers at 0, 0.17, 0.42 and 0.55 s, steady at 0.67 s); a loupe already on a plate, rising to reveal the table; a hand-written date on an envelope filling the frame. - **Endings**: the index of everything on the table; the last photograph held in depth with one line of text; the loupe landing on today's name and contact.

# Archive light table: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.7, medium 2.5, long 4.2.

## hook

- en: glide over the table, a loupe drops onto a glass plate inside growing crop corners, the negative turns positive from the centre
- id: kamera meluncur di meja, lup turun ke pelat kaca di antara sudut bidik, negatif berubah jadi positif dari tengah lensa

## problem

- en: the loupe lands on the damage, a broken corner or faded line, ringed in the signal colour; a dark plate names the loss
- id: lup mendarat di bagian rusak, sudut patah atau tulisan pudar, dilingkari warna sinyal; pelat gelap menyebut masalahnya

## fact

- en: dive through the lens until the photo fills the frame; an ink leader rises from a signal anchor to a serif title
- id: kamera menyelam ke lensa sampai foto penuh; garis tinta naik dari titik jangkar ke judul serif

## step

- en: glide from plate to plate in date order; each catalogue tag fades in as the camera first meets its object
- id: kamera meluncur dari pelat ke pelat sesuai urutan tanggal; label katalog muncul saat kamera tiba di bendanya

## compare

- en: two plates side by side, each with a caption plate quoting its source, held still until both are read
- id: dua pelat berdampingan, masing-masing dengan pelat keterangan dan sumbernya, diam sampai keduanya terbaca

## number

- en: a dark reading plate wipes in from its edge; the mono figure counts up from zero, the source line below
- id: pelat bacaan gelap diusap masuk; angka mono dihitung dari nol, sumbernya tertulis di bawah

## proof

- en: inside the lens one line of a document lights up left to right, an underline draws, its figure is ringed and lifted out
- id: di dalam lensa satu baris dokumen menyala dari kiri, garis bawah ditarik, angkanya dilingkari lalu diangkat keluar

## offer

- en: the loupe lands on today's object beside the old ones; its name sits in a dark plate with a signal edge
- id: lup turun ke benda masa kini di samping arsip lama; namanya di pelat gelap bertepi warna sinyal

## cta

- en: rise out, glide to the last plate, the loupe lands on the name; name and contact in a caption plate, held 2 s
- id: naik keluar lensa, meluncur ke pelat terakhir, lup mendarat di papan nama; nama dan kontak diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: pull back to the whole table, every plate with its catalogue tag; one line of text, held 2 s
- id: kamera mundur memperlihatkan seluruh meja, tiap pelat dengan label katalognya; satu kalimat, diam 2 detik
